answer: Each identity claims one dye vat marked by a relic stone filed once, posts an 80-credit bond, and files juniper wood weight, saffron weight, and bath volume for fuel and batch. Auditor remeasures vat and batch, recomputes saffron dye strength from the public table by weight, volume, and juniper ash, and burns the bond if strength outside 5 percent, relic code repeats, or one marker covers two vats. First pays 36, kth 36+5(k-1), 1000th 5031, so 1000 fakes pay 2,533,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-dye ring fails on remeasurement; an honest dyer pays 36 once, bond back after one epoch.
